newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's TV3 raises annual net profit to C$23.15 mln.
newsitem.headline: NZ's TV3 raises annual net profit to C$23.15 mln.

text.p: New Zealand's Canadian-owned TV3 network said on Wednesday its net earnings totalled C$23.15 million in the year to June, 1996, up sharply from C$9.65 million a year earlier.
TV3 managing director Graeme Hunter said it was the channel's most profitable year to date.

Over the year, TV3's share of the key age group -- the 18 to 49 year-old audience - rose by nine percent, providing the network with advertising revenue growth considerably ahead of the total television market.
TV3 installed more than 25 transmitter and translater sites throughout New Zealand during the year, with coverage now approaching 97 percent of the population.

"Our first quarter to March has shown a further 11 percent prime time audience growth in the key 18-49 demographic (sector)," he said, adding the Superleague rugby league competition had kicked off with strong ratings.
"We've had a good first quarter in a pretty tough market," Hunter told Reuters, adding the company was on track for a June 29 launch of its entertainment-based channel, TV4.
CanWest Global Communications' owns 68 percent of TV3 and plans to go to full control this year.
CanWest last week said its earnings for the six months to February were up 28 percent at C$33.9 million.
TV3's contribution to total revenue of C$407.3 million was C$45.28 million, up from C$22.75 million a year earlier.
